name: ConceptBase.cc
tagline: Deductive object base for metamodeling, built on O-Telos with Datalog rules and unlimited meta-levels.
description: ConceptBase.cc is a multi-user deductive object base that implements O-Telos, a variant of the Telos knowledge-representation language. Everything is a proposition and instantiation is a relation rather than a fixed layer, so one database can hold example data, schemas, metaclasses and meta-metaclasses together; integrity constraints, deductive rules evaluated by a Datalog engine, event-condition-action rules and recursive functions all work across those levels. That makes it a specialised tool for designing and analysing modeling languages and for method engineering rather than a general application database. Developed since 1987 at Passau, Aachen, Tilburg and now the University of Skövde, it is still maintained: version 8.5.16 shipped in July 2026 with a Linux server and a Java graph-editor client under a FreeBSD-style license.

scale.notes: Sized for models and metamodels rather than bulk application data.

strengths: Unlimited classification levels: data, classes, metaclasses and beyond in one store
Deductive rules and integrity constraints apply uniformly across meta-levels
ECA active rules and recursive functions for model analysis
Graph editor client whose node and link rendering is itself defined by rules
Still actively maintained, with regular releases
weaknesses: Built for metamodeling, not high-volume application data
Steep learning curve around Telos and O-Telos concepts
useCases: Designing and validating domain-specific modeling languages
Method engineering and multi-level modeling research
Teaching conceptual modeling and deductive databases
